newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Nobel laureate dismisses Suharto trip to E. Timor.
newsitem.headline: Nobel laureate dismisses Suharto trip to E. Timor.

text.p: East Timorese resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta, awarded the Nobel peace prize last week, on Tuesday dismissed a visit to his homeland by Indonesian President Suharto as a publicity stunt.
Suharto was to visit the former Portuguese colony on Tuesday to unveil a 27-metre statue of Jesus Christ.

Ramos-Horta, who fled three days before Indonesia invaded East Timor in December 1975 and has since acted as the resistance movement's international spokesman, said the statue's height was a reference to the 27 provinces claimed by Indonesia -- including East Timor.
To reinforce the point, there were 27 steps leading up to the statue itself, Ramos-Horta told a news conference in Sydney.

"We know that Jesus Christ was not 27 metres tall and it is simply a joke in poor taste for Indonesia to do this," said Ramos-Horta, who shared the 1996 peace prize with East Timor's outspoken Catholic bishop, Carlos Belo.
"We believe it is a publicity stunt to signal Indonesia's sovereignty over East Timor, to prevent or counter international support for East Timor," he added. "But we believe it is backfiring."
